newsitem.title: UK: Anglian says windfall tax will be legal-paper.
newsitem.headline: Anglian says windfall tax will be legal-paper.

text.p: Anglian Water Plc said the British government's planned windfall tax on privatised companies was likely to be legal, the Times newspaper said on Thursday.
But Anglian Water added that any such levy would mean less cash for investment and delays in consumer price cuts, the paper said.
The ruling Labour Party has long said it will impose a levy on formerly state-owned utilities, saying they had been laxly regulated and sold off too cheaply, allowing excess profits.

Although the government has been at pains since the May 1 election not to identify which companies would be hit by the tax, electricity and water companies were widely seen at the fore of those likely to be affected.

Privatised companies in other sectors, such as British Telecom and airport operator BAA, have said this month that they either should not have the tax imposed on them or that they will fight the legality of what would be a retrospective tax.
Anglian Water on Wednesday announced annual pre-tax profits of 257 million pounds, up from a prior 237 million pounds, with the dividend at 34.5 pence stg from 30 pence.
Its share price lost 0.5 pence to 682 pence on Wednesday after whipsawing in a 20 pence range topped by a 695 pence high.
